**Verdict: PASS. No new findings** for DG2 round 4. The D-064 repairs still respect the playbook, and all 26 assigned requirements are met on candidate `sha256:29ced0ed…ce58`.

**Candidate check.** Recomputing the candidate ID gives the same value in the repository and in my disposable clone (521 files). HEAD is `bb4dd9c9`, not the source commit `e37f6ea4`, but it descends from it and the only changes since are delivery metadata (the round-4 assignments, the manifest and `stages.json`). The historical DG1 validation passes.

**Your three questions about the blank-text rule:**
- **Does any playbook field legitimately need text the rule now refuses?** No. Every playbook fill-in (charter fields, the four-part thesis, the T01–T04 columns, the scope-check evidence) expects real content, and none gives meaning to spaces, invisible format characters or fillers.
  - Visible text is still accepted exactly as typed, including Arabic text with a direction mark and emoji sequences. Short values like "-", "N/A" and "0" are accepted.
  - An empty field still means "no value", and clearing a field still works.
- **Is the guidance clear in both languages?** Yes. The inline message is "Enter some text; spaces alone are not a value." / "أدخِل نصاً؛ المسافات وحدها ليست قيمة.". I watched it live in English (left-to-right) and Arabic (right-to-left): the field is marked invalid, gets focus, and nothing is sent. For invisible characters the message says "spaces", but the field looks empty, so it still reads correctly. I didn't raise this as a finding.
- **Do the B0041 pre-check, G1–G3 readiness and the thesis flag still work?**
  - The API refuses an Out of scope made only of invisible characters. When I planted such values straight into the database, the exclusions pre-check still failed and G1's initial-charter item stayed incomplete.
  - An invisible-only thesis part planted in the database raises the thesis-incomplete warning, and restoring real text clears it.
  - G1, G2 and G3 must be approved in order. In the live run the Sponsor approved them in turn and the phase moved diagnose → define → design → mobilize. These were demo decisions on synthetic data, not real approvals.

**Checks run (all exit 0):**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Typecheck, build, lint (Node 22 and 24) | exit 0 on both |
| Unit tests (Node 22 and 24) | 616/616 on both |
| Contrast check (Node 22 and 24) | 50 pairs meet WCAG AA on both |
| Integration tests on a disposable PostgreSQL (Node 24) | 465/465 |
| Product browser journeys, English and Arabic, with accessibility checks | 40/40 |
| My own charter blank and invisible-text browser check, English and Arabic | 12/12 |
| Live API scenario | 83/83 |

**Invariants:**
- Nothing claims PMI or Mobily certification, and the brand badge reads "Provisional" / "مؤقت".
- The only engineering-gate (DG0–DG7) mention in product code is a note saying product gates are unrelated to them.
- Unquantified value pools show no amount rather than 0, and money columns are decimal.

**Things to know:**
- **First live run failed, my fault:** G2 was refused because my own database planting script bumped the charter version without a matching version row. That is my test-script error, not a product defect. I fixed the script and the re-run passes 83/83; this is written down in `env.txt`.
- **Handback in a different place:** the write guard blocked the assigned handback path (`docs/delivery/handbacks/DG2/…`) for my role. I put it at `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/domain/round-4/handback-T-DG2-REV-DOM-R4-domain-reviewer.md` instead; you may want to copy it across.
- **Environmental items recorded as PASS, as instructed:** the live package registry (D-057), live CI (D-058) and Keycloak (D-049) were checked offline or locally only, with the residual named in each record.

The review record passes schema validation with zero errors, and all 60 evidence paths exist. I removed the disposable clone and scratch files afterwards.

- `reviews/DG2/round-4/domain-reviewer.md`
